what_is_forecast: Whether SWS involuntary hunger in Balance Luzon (Luzon outside Metro Manila) in the target quarter will be significantly above its five-year normal (beyond the survey margin of error).
geographic_scope: Balance Luzon (regional). CALABARZON is ~34% of its population. Not a CALABARZON, provincial or municipal measurement or forecast.
measurement_type: forecast of a directly measured regional survey outcome (experience-based hunger), not observed prevalence

forecast.probability_note: In the walk-forward test, 3 past forecasts fell in the 0.4-0.6 range and 100% of them were followed by a HIGH quarter (mean forecast 46%). Few cases: read the probability as approximate.
forecast.interval_note: Range method: errors of past out-of-sample forecasts (conformal). It contained the published result in 97% of 62 past quarters. The projected number is the latest reading drifting toward normal, not a model of causes.
forecast.class_rule: HIGH is raised when the probability is at least 0.12, the threshold that best balanced missed HIGH quarters and false alarms in training (fixed in FI7)

baseline_comparison.statement: Over 62 past quarters this outlook was no better than simply carrying the latest reading forward (Brier score 0.118 vs 0.115; lower is better). It is a structured persistence forecast, not a demonstrated gain in skill.

limitations: Regional only: Balance Luzon, of which CALABARZON is about a third. Not a CALABARZON, provincial or LGU figure.
Provisional: not reliable once the alternating survey quarters are set aside, and not better than persistence.
Only 11 HIGH quarters since 2010; the recall estimate could plausibly be anywhere from 0 to 0.8.
SWS release dates before 2021 follow a rule, not the recorded release, which affects the historical scores.
The first untouched test is this forecast itself, scored when the target quarter's SWS result is published.
survey_design_note: The latest reading came from a round with 600 Balance Luzon respondents. Since 2023, rounds with 300 respondents have read about 5 points lower than larger rounds, so part of the quarter-to-quarter swing is survey design, not hunger.
explanation: The outlook carries forward the latest SWS reading for Balance Luzon (23.6%, 2026-Q3) and lets it drift back toward the five-year normal (16.2%) by the fitted factor 0.67 per quarter. The significantly-above-normal line is 20.2%. No other indicator changes this number: at this issue date no domain or news input improved the forecast or beat the latest reading. News did improve a LightGBM model's probabilities when issued on the last day of the quarter, but that model was still not better than the latest reading (docs/fi9n).

domain_context.note: Latest values known on the issue date, shown as context. They are not inputs of the served model, and the ablation found no measurable Lead-1 contribution from any of them.
